fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's installer columnist says turf between concrete, pavers, travertine or flagstone goes in with fewer callbacks when large sections are laid over the hardscape and cut out around it, rather than pieced in as strips, even though it wastes more turf.
quote: Placing synthetic turf in between concrete, pavers, travertine, or flagstone can magnify the beauty of the projects design. Placing synthetic turf ribbons in between these type of hardscapes can be challenging. … The client should be informed about the waste and cost it will take in order for the installation of turf ribbons to be installed correctly. … In the long run you will save labor costs and call backs by using large sections of turf and cutting out the hardscape instead of using pieces and strips. … Depending on the size of the project you can actually save days of labor and materials by using large sections instead of seam tape and gluing sections and pieces together.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Installing Artificial Grass Between Pavers (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)
notes: Synthetic Grass Warehouse is a turf distributor; 'Ask JW' is its installer-training column (JW). Page datePublished 2016-06-08, dateModified 2022-12-29 (schema.org). Read with curl on 2026-09-25.

fact: The same column says hardscape contractors often set concrete, pavers, travertine, marble or flagstone on a concrete bed or a poured concrete edge, which gets in the way of both the turf's compacted base and its fasteners, so the edge line should be agreed with the hardscape contractor first; otherwise the concrete is saw-cut or the turf is anchored to it with concrete fasteners.
quote: Contractors that place concrete, pavers, travertine, marble or flagstone rock will place the hardscape over a concrete bed or an exterior poured in place concrete edge to structurally hold the hardscape in place. This exterior concreted edge will cause difficulty in placing the correct amount of compacted imported subgrade materials to install the turf on. This exterior concrete edge will also cause difficulty securing the turf ribbons. It is advantageous to communicate with the hardscape contractor prior to the installation to ensure the edge of hardscape will not run past the line of your nailing edge. If this happens you will need to either saw cut or remove the overflow of the concrete, or drill and conset (drill and anchor) the turf ribbons with concrete fasteners.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Installing Artificial Grass Between Pavers (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)

fact: The column warns that turf ribbons in flat or level hardscape with little or no positive drainage can flood, and says the compacted drainage fill in each joint must finish no more than 1/2 inch below all the hardscape, to avoid trip hazards, and be compacted to at least 80% or the ribbons settle.
quote: Installing turf ribbons within flat or level hardscapes that have minimum or no positive drainage can lead to flooding and an unhappy client. … The elevation of the drainage fill must be no more than 1/2 inch below all hardscape after compaction. This will prevent any trip hazards or toe stubbing after years of foot traffic. … If the drainage fill is not compacted at least 80% the turf ribbons will settle over time and you will have to remove and replace and start all over again.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Installing Artificial Grass Between Pavers (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)
notes: The column does not say what the 80% is measured against (Proctor or otherwise); quote it as the columnist's figure.

fact: The column suggests planning ribbon layouts with the hardscape contractor in 15-foot increments to cut waste, laying the turf with its fibers toward the focal point, and lining up each section's gauge rows.
quote: If you work hand and hand with the hardscape contractor you can educate his sales team about the lay-out of the designed ribbons in 15 feet increments. This will allow having to piece in small sections of cutting off unnecessary waste. … I recommend laying the synthetic turf sections where the fibers face toward the focal point. … When the sections are placed make sure that each sections gauges line up so that there is no difference in alignment.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Installing Artificial Grass Between Pavers (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)

fact: The column lets the turf settle over the hardscape for at least an hour, nails the middle of each ribbon about a foot apart so nothing shifts during cutting, cuts along each stone's edge and lifts out the turf over the stone, and says ribbon edges take many nails, with small heads that hide in the fibers.
quote: Place and align sections over hardscape and allow to sit for at least an hour. … Place spikes/nails in the center of each ribbon approximately 1′ apart. This will prevent the turf sections from moving during cutting. … Follow the edge of the hardscape cutting the turf along the edge until you reach back to the starting point of cutting. Remove the middle section and move on to the next area to be cut out. … When installing turf ribbons it requires many nails to secure the edge. The less manipulation and smaller nail head will hide nail placement.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Installing Artificial Grass Between Pavers (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)
notes: The column's nail sizes and spacings (40d and 16d) belong to artificial-turf-nails-vs-staples; this page cites only the method.

fact: The column recommends a smaller infill spread slowly by hand in ribbons, because a drop spreader traps fibers under too much infill, and warns that heavy brushing lifts ribbon edges and pulls out edge nails, so it uses a stiff hand brush and a power broom only on wide ribbons.
quote: Since the area of ribbons are small I recommend placing smaller infill. Infill by hand or stay focused on the amount of infill dropped at one time. Using a drop spreader will lesson controllability and will cause the turf fibers to be trapped by placing too much infill. … Excessive brushing and fibrillating will cause the edges to lift and extracting of the edge nails. I would take a stiff hand brush and brush the fibers vertical. If the ribbons are big enough then a power broom may be used.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Installing Artificial Grass Between Pavers (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)

fact: A Synthetic Grass Warehouse article says the base between pavers is built like any turf base, except that compaction is harder in a narrow gap, where it suggests a stamp compactor or a piece of wood and a hammer.
quote: Installing a sub-base for turf ribbons is much the same as a typical artificial turf installation. The only significant difference is that compaction can be more difficult when you’re working with such a narrow area. Ideally, use a stamp compactor to compact the turf base between pavers. You can also compact the base manually using a piece of wood and a hammer if you don’t have access to a stamp compactor.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Critical Steps for Installing Artificial Turf Between Pavers (April 29, 2024)
notes: Synthetic Grass Warehouse is a turf distributor. Article datePublished 2024-04-29 (schema.org). Read with curl on 2026-09-25.

fact: The article says to spray water over the area between the pavers first to find where it puddles, that a concrete or rock area must be graded or drilled so the turf can drain, and that turf over hardscape such as concrete is glued with turf adhesive, not nailed.
quote: To check the drainage, spray water over the area. If there are any pools or puddles that form, there are areas that will need to be addressed. If the ground is dirt or soil, you can move on to the next step of installing a sub-base layer. If the area is concrete, cement, or rock, however, you’ll need to grade the concrete layer or drill holes to ensure proper drainage for your artificial turf installation. … If you’re adhering your turf grass onto hardscaping such as concrete, you’ll need to use artificial grass adhesive rather than landscaping nails.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Critical Steps for Installing Artificial Turf Between Pavers (April 29, 2024)

fact: The article says to unroll the turf with every fiber facing one way, usually toward the house, to cut each piece 1 to 2 inches oversize on each side for trimming and securing, and to seam strips with their fibers facing the same direction.
quote: Start by unrolling the turf, ensuring all fibers are facing the desired direction. Typically, the most aesthetically pleasing orientation is with the turf blades facing the property. Once you have the turf laid out, cut it to the perfect size for your paver gap, leaving an extra 1-2 inches on each side for trimming and securing. … Start by laying the turf strips next to each other with the fibers facing the same direction.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Critical Steps for Installing Artificial Turf Between Pavers (April 29, 2024)

fact: CMHA's construction guide builds a paver patio as one interlocking surface: pavers on a nominal 1 inch of bedding sand over a compacted base sloped at least 1.5%, joints kept between 1/16 and 3/16 inch and filled with sand, bedding sand never used to make up for an uneven base, and no more than 1/8 inch of lippage between pavers on a walking route.
quote: Slopes should be a minimum of 1.5%. … Bedding sand should be spread and screeded to an uncompacted nominal 1 in. (25 mm) thickness. Frozen or saturated sand should not be installed. If there is an uneven base (due to inconsistent compaction or improper grading), the bedding sand should not be used to compensate for it. Over time, unevenness in the bedding sand will reflect through to the surface. … Joint widths between the pavers should be consistent and be between 1/16 and 3/16 in. (2 and 5 mm). … Dry joint sand is spread into the joints and the pavers compacted again until the joints are full. … Lippage between individual pavers should be a maximum 1/8 in. (3 mm) for pedestrian access routes.
source_label: Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association, PAV-TEC-002-22 Construction of Interlocking Concrete Pavements (revised 2022)
notes: CMHA succeeded the Interlocking Concrete Pavement Institute (ICPI). Web tech note carries the code PAV-TEC-002-22. Read with curl on 2026-09-25.

fact: CMHA's guide for concrete paving slabs says slabs don't interlock or pass loads to their neighbors through joint sand, so it asks for a flatter base than under pavers, within 1/4 inch over a 10-foot straightedge, sloped at least 1.5% and compacted to at least 98% of standard Proctor density.
quote: Installed base surface tolerances should be ± 1/4 in. (6 mm) over a 10 ft (3 m) straightedge. This tolerance is tighter than the ± 3/8 in. (10 mm) over a 10 ft (3 m) straightedge for interlocking concrete pavements. The reason for the tighter base surface tolerance for slabs is to provide a more uniform support and help prevent vertical movement due to lack of interlock among the paving units. Bases should slope a minimum of 1.5% for drainage. The installed density should be at least 98% of standard Proctor density per ASTM D698. … Paving slabs do not interlock and therefore do not spread loads to their neighbors via joint sand.
source_label: Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association, PAV-TEC-025-22 Construction Guidelines for Segmental Concrete Paving Slabs and Planks in Pedestrian Applications
notes: Page carries the code PAV-TEC-025-22 (schema.org dateModified 2024-12-12). ASTM C1782 defines a slab as a unit with more than 101 sq in of face and a length-to-thickness ratio over four. Read with curl on 2026-09-25.

fact: CMHA says mortar bedding under paving slabs suits pedestrian areas in freezing climates only when it is fortified with a latex or epoxy additive, because mortar can be damaged by de-icers.
quote: Mortar bedding can be used in pedestrian applications in nonfreezing climates and in freezing climates if fortified with a latex or epoxy additive as mortar can be susceptible to damage and deterioration from deicers.
source_label: Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association, PAV-TEC-025-22 Construction Guidelines for Segmental Concrete Paving Slabs and Planks in Pedestrian Applications

fact: CMHA says slabs on a compacted aggregate base and bedding sand are for pedestrians or light automobile traffic, that heavier traffic calls for a concrete or asphalt base, and that in permeable paving, where joints are wide, slabs 16 by 16 inches and larger belong in pedestrian areas only because under vehicles they risk tipping and cracking.
quote: Applications on compacted aggregate bases and bedding sand are for pedestrian or light automobile traffic with limited trucks. For additional vehicular traffic loads, slabs and planks should generally be installed on bedding sand over a concrete or asphalt base. … Slabs 16 x 16 in. (400 x 400 mm) and larger should be limited to pedestrian uses only and their minimum thickness should be 3.125 in. (80 mm). Using 16 x 16 in. or larger units in vehicular applications risks tipping and cracking. … These units have wider joints (typically filled with No. 8 or 89 stone) than non-permeable applications in order to receive stormwater runoff.
source_label: Concrete Masonry & Hardscapes Association, PAV-TEC-025-22 Construction Guidelines for Segmental Concrete Paving Slabs and Planks in Pedestrian Applications
